thread:
Maya (Customer Success): @channel ACME reported a regression in non-English outputs after last night's rollout. They say their Portuguese customer-facing translations started returning English or garbled text. Ticket: https://acme.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/42311 :warning:

Jorge (Support): CC @Li and @Priya — they pasted an example. They call the endpoint with model=redwood-v2.2 and temperature=0.0. Before rollout the same prompt returned fluent Portuguese. Now it returns English or mixes languages.

acme-integration: customer message -> 'Por favor traduza o seguinte para português: "Our onboarding flow is delayed by two steps"'

acme-integration: current API response -> 'Our onboarding flow is delayed by two steps.'

Maya (Customer Success): reproducible for them across several inputs and also observed for Arabic/Hindi examples in the same workspace. Started ~2025-11-29 23:40 UTC which aligns with the canary promotion.

Jorge (Support): repro steps (from customer):
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
   -d '{"model":"redwood-v2.2","input":"Por favor traduza para português: \"Our onboarding flow is delayed by two steps\"","temperature":0.0}'
2) expect Portuguese output, get English

Jorge (Support): attached the raw response (trimmed):
```
{"id":"resp_789","output":[{"type":"text","text":"Our onboarding flow is delayed by two steps."}],"meta":{"model":"redwood-v2.2","version":"2025-11-29-rc3"}}
```

Li (ML Eng): thanks, good repro. Quick questions: did they pin to a specific variant? customer said they didn't pin, using catalog default. Do we know rollout id pushed last night?

Omar (SRE): deploy-bot shows canary rollout #2025-11-29-rc3 -> promoted to 60% at 23:35 UTC, full at 01:10 UTC for hosted. Logs show no 500s. No infra errors.

Priya (Oncall): assigning to @Li for model behavior. For immediate mitigation we can pin workspace to previous model version (redwood-v2.1) via tenant-config. Maya can propose that to ACME as a short-term fix.

Maya (Customer Success): shared a tenant-config snippet they can use: 
```
POST /v1/tenants/acme/config
{ "default_model": "redwood-v2.1" }
```
They asked if that will require downtime. Jorge: no downtime, config changes apply immediately.

Li (ML Eng): initial hypothesis: decoding change in v2.2 RC3 - we adjusted fallback heuristics for short prompts which might be collapsing language detection for prompts that embed the target language in English but ask to translate. Another possibility: a tokenizer mapping tweak that affects language tokens. Will run a compare between v2.1 and v2.2 on a small multilingual prompt set.

Jorge (Support): customer reports similar behavior when prompt is 'Traduza isto para português:' vs 'Por favor traduza para português:' — inconsistent.

Li (ML Eng): can you paste two failing payloads and the full response objects (including meta fields)? Need the model version string and decode settings. Also pinging @SRE for request traces (trace id).

acme-integration: provided trace id: trace_0b12f9e4, request ts 2025-11-29T23:41:03Z.

Omar (SRE): trace lookup shows request routed to pool-gpu-a, kernel-stack v3.1, decode-config: {"beam":1,"temperature":0.0,"language_detection":true,"token_bias":{}}. No memory pressure.

Li (ML Eng): interesting: language_detection=true was turned on as part of a small change to improve multilingual fallback. That flag got enabled by default in rc3. Could be it returns a detected-language override and then decodes in target language only when detection is confident. For short translation prompts detection may be low-confidence and we fallback to source language (English).

Priya (Oncall): immediate mitigation options:
- Pin customer to v2.1 (low effort)
- Disable language_detection default for rc3 (requires a patched rollout)
- Add a recommended prompt hack (prepend: '\\nLanguage: PT-BR' or explicit system message) while we patch.

Maya (Customer Success): ACME agreed to pin to v2.1 for now. They asked for ETA on root cause and fix.

Li (ML Eng): plan: reproduce locally on a small suite, confirm hypothesis, and prepare a targeted patch to revert language_detection default or adjust confidence threshold. ETA: initial repro and writeup in 4-6 hours, patch in 24-36 hours depending on canary cycle.

Jorge (Support): I told the customer: pinned and will update when ML posts a root-cause. They appreciated fast mitigation :thumbsup:.

Maya (Customer Success): documenting SLA impact: translation quality regression only, no request failures, billing unaffected. Marking as P2 per CS triage.

Li (ML Eng): adding a short-term test matrix we will run: Portuguese, Spanish, Arabic, Hindi, Chinese prompts across prompt prefixes: 'Traduza para', 'Please translate to', 'Por favor traduza', plus variations. Also test short vs longer input.

Omar (SRE): flagging monitoring: add a dashboard for 'non-English output rate' by tenant over time (baseline -> we can detect spikes). I'll create a metric: proportion_of_responses_language!=requested_lang.

Maya (Customer Success): noted. I'll update the Zendesk ticket and let ACME know pinned and we have an ML investigation underway. Ticket updated: https://acme.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/42311 (comment added).

Li (ML Eng): assigning internal issue RI-ML-5423 and will post PR link when available.

Priya (Oncall): if anyone sees customer reporting for other tenants escalate immediately.

Jorge (Support): thanks all. I'll keep this thread updated with any new examples from ACME. :eyes:

deploy-bot: rollout #2025-11-29-rc3 -> status: promoted to 60% at 2025-11-29T23:35:22Z, promoted to 100% at 2025-11-30T01:10:09Z

Maya (Customer Success): closing loop for now — mitigation applied, owner @Li, SRE monitoring metric in flight. Will reopen if customer sees recurrence. :white_check_mark:
